title: GEOSPATIAL MODELLING FOR PUBLIC HEALTH APPLICATIONS
text:
The Geospatial Modelling Workshop is an intensive training programme for statisticians and public health professionals looking to build their skills in geospatial analysis and modelling. Drawing on real-life examples from malaria research, the programme guides participants from foundational spatial data concepts through to Bayesian geostatistical modelling — equipping them with skills they can continue to build on long after the training ends.
The workshop is run annually, bringing together leading researchers and practitioners from across the region.

title: Dr. Susan Rumisha
text:
Principal Research Scientist; Lead, Malaria Atlas Project (MAP) Dar es Salaam Node, Ifakara Health Institute
Dr. Rumisha specializes in developing geospatial analytical frameworks for malaria, with a focus on producing malaria risk maps, estimating disease burden, and evaluating malaria health systems. She is driven by the use of data-driven evidence to strengthen malaria decision-making.
She is affiliated with the National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR) in Tanzania, the Telethon Kids Institute, and Curtin University in Perth, WA, Australia.

title: Dr. Ousmane Diao
text:
Senior Research Scientist, MAP Dar es Salaam Node, Ifakara Health Institute
Dr. Diao’s expertise spans mathematical engineering, geospatial modelling, and malaria epidemiology. He develops and implements spatiotemporal models to estimate malaria, assess transmission profiles, and evaluate intervention strategies. He has contributed to capacity strengthening through teaching and training in geospatial modelling across Africa, including the Malaria Modelling training school (MaMOD) and MAP ECR training programmes.
He holds a PhD in Mathematical Engineering from UCLouvain, Belgium, and an MSc in Bioinformatics/Biomathematics from UCAD, Senegal, and has published widely on malaria and infectious disease modelling.

title: Dr. Amina Msengwa
text:
Senior Lecturer, Department of Statistics, University of Dar es Salaam
With more than two decades of teaching and research experience, Dr. Msengwa’s expertise spans epidemiology, biostatistics, Bayesian statistics, and spatial statistics. She has made significant contributions to understanding and mapping disease burden in Tanzania, and is dedicated to applying statistical models across health and environmental domains.

title: Dr. Punam Amratia
text:
Senior Research Scientist; Technical Lead, MAP Dar es Salaam Node, Ifakara Health Institute
With over a decade of experience in malaria epidemiology, biostatistics, and geospatial modelling, Dr. Amratia has made significant contributions to understanding and mapping malaria risk and burden. She also teaches data science courses at the University of Oxford and has supported capacity strengthening in numerous malaria-endemic countries.
She holds an MSc in Epidemiology from Imperial College London and a PhD in Emerging Pathogens from the University of Florida.

title: Programme Overview
text:
Geostatistical models are increasingly important in public health research due to the rise in spatial health data. This intensive course suits statisticians and public health professionals wanting to enhance their skills in geospatial analysis and modelling. Participants learn about spatial data structures and geostatistics through real-life examples, progressing from basic to complex models using Bayesian inference with the INLA approach.
The focus is on spatial patterns of malaria and other health outcomes, with an emphasis on skills that continue to develop after the course.

title: Programme Overview
text:
Who Should Apply
This course is designed for statisticians and public health professionals who want to build their geospatial analysis and modelling skills. Candidates should have:

Basic experience with R
An understanding of statistical inference
Introductory knowledge of Bayesian statistical methods

title: Programme Overview
text:
Format



Duration
Typically a three-day intensive training.



Instructors
Leading experts in geospatial modelling and public health.



Teaching Method
A mix of lectures and hands-on practicals, using real-life examples drawn from malaria research.



Software
R (version 4.0 and above).



Language
English.

title: Programme Overview
text:
What You’ll Learn
Lecture topics include:

Introduction to Geostatistics
Spatial Data in R
Areal Data and Models
Geostatistical Models in INLA
Basics of Point Process Models (where time allows)
